clue.text: Snare ten squirming fish

indicators.note: squirming suggests wriggling about, so the letters of the word ten are jumbled

parts.note: to fish with rod and line is to angle

explanation.surface: Someone trying to catch ten wriggling fish in a trap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'squirming' rearranges TEN into ENT; 'fish' looks like a noun but is the verb ANGLE.
explanation.definitionFit: To snare something is to trap it so it is caught up and tangled.

clue.text: Electronic equipment likely to go in cut

indicators.note: to go in tells us one word is placed inside another here

parts.note: to lop is to cut off
apt means likely, as in apt to happen

explanation.surface: Gadgets that are likely to be cut from a budget.
explanation.definitionFit: A portable computer is a common piece of electronic equipment.

clue.text: Artisan whose work caused feathers to fly

definitions.text: Artisan whose work caused feathers to fly

parts.words: Artisan whose work caused feathers to fly
parts.note: a maker of arrows fixes feathers to the shafts, and those feathered arrows then fly through the air

explanation.surface: A craftsman whose work set off a flurry of feathers, as in a squabble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'feathers to fly' sounds like the idiom for a row, but here the fletched arrows literally fly.
explanation.definitionFit: An arrow-maker's craft is fitting feathered flights to arrows, which are then shot.

clue.text: City's side at sea in scoreless draw

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', so the city is what the wordplay builds

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other here

parts.note: a nil-nil draw is written 0-0, two Os
port is the left-hand side of a ship

explanation.surface: A football club's side playing badly in a goalless draw.
explanation.walkthrough: 'City' and 'side' suggest a football team; the side is a ship's.
explanation.definitionFit: Oporto is the Portuguese city famous for port wine, also called Porto.

clue.text: Production of woods for indoor bowls

definitions.text: Production of woods for indoor bowls

parts.words: Production of woods for indoor bowls
parts.note: growing miniature trees, little woods, in shallow pots kept indoors

explanation.surface: Making wooden balls for the indoor game of bowls.
explanation.walkthrough: In the game of bowls the balls are called 'woods'; here the woods are tiny trees and the bowls are pots.
explanation.definitionFit: The Japanese art of growing dwarf trees in shallow containers is exactly a production of small woods in bowls.

clue.text: Important person for an important lecture

definitions.meaning: read as two words, a big wigging: a serious telling-off

explanation.walkthrough: 'Wigging' is British slang for a telling-off.
explanation.definitionFit: A grandee is a big wheel, and a wigging is a scolding, so a big one is a stern lecture.

clue.text: Backward students demonstrate human fallibility

indicators.note: backward tells us to read the word for students from end to start

parts.note: pupils are students at school

explanation.surface: Slow learners show that people make mistakes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backward students' looks like slow pupils; 'Backward' is the turnaround signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To make a small mistake shows that people are fallible.

clue.text: Quietly mention favour

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical direction for quietly
to refer to something is to mention it

explanation.surface: Asking softly for a favour.
explanation.definitionFit: To favour one option is to like it better than others.

clue.text: Make wealth the wrong way?

parts.note: getting rich by crime; also, smashing up the letters of the law gives wealth

explanation.surface: Getting rich by dishonest means.
explanation.walkthrough: A second reading: break up the letters of 'the law' and they spell 'wealth'.
explanation.definitionFit: Committing a crime is a wrong way to get money, and breaking the letters of the law makes wealth.

clue.text: Taken aback by swindles, tag was changed outside

indicators.note: outside puts the rearranged letters around another piece
was changed means the letters of tag are rearranged

parts.note: to have someone is to swindle them, so he has means he swindles

explanation.surface: Shocked at being cheated, someone finds a price tag altered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swindles' reads as a noun but is the verb, as in 'he has you' for cheating; 'was changed' scrambles the second word into AGT before it goes round.
explanation.definitionFit: Being aghast is being shocked, struck with horror, which is being taken aback.

clue.text: Honoured by the electorate, dishonoured by the bank

definitions.meaning: an MP re-elected is sent back to Parliament
a bounced cheque is sent back unpaid by the bank

explanation.definitionFit: A cheque the bank refuses is sent back, and a candidate re-elected is sent back to office.

clue.text: Elevator for part of the building

definitions.meaning: something that lifts, here an aircraft's lifting surface
an extension or section to one side of a building

explanation.walkthrough: 'Elevator' suggests a lift in the building; it is the part of a plane that gives lift.
explanation.definitionFit: An aircraft's aerofoil gives lift, and a section of a large house or hospital is also called this.

clue.text: Weapon to quicken the pulse

parts.note: pulse is the vegetable kind, dried peas, which a toy tube fires off quickly

explanation.surface: A thrilling gun that sets the heart racing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pulse' means peas, beans and lentils, not a heartbeat.
explanation.definitionFit: A child's tube for blowing dried peas at targets is a toy weapon that sends pulses flying.

clue.text: Break alternative arrangements

indicators.note: arrangements of a word's letters signal an anagram here

explanation.surface: Taking time out to consider alternative plans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arrangements' shuffles the letters of 'alternative'. TEA INTERVAL is the afternoon break in a cricket match.
explanation.definitionFit: A pause for refreshments in a cricket match is a scheduled break.

clue.text: One's fiancée proposed

definitions.meaning: the person one is engaged to marry
planned or meant, as in the proposed route

explanation.definitionFit: A betrothed partner is called this, and something planned or purposed is also described this way.

clue.text: None left unharmed

definitions.meaning: jokily, if nothing is on the left, everything is on the other side

explanation.definitionFit: Someone unharmed is fine and okay; whimsically, with none on the left, the lot is on the right.

clue.text: Lorraine's French companion

parts.note: Lorraine is a French region always paired with its neighbour in a hyphenated name

explanation.surface: A woman called Lorraine and her French friend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lorraine' looks like a woman's name; it is the French region, paired in Alsace-Lorraine.
explanation.definitionFit: The two eastern French regions are linked as Alsace-Lorraine, so one is the other's partner.

clue.text: Unambiguous order

explanation.definitionFit: Plain speaking is straightforward, and to instruct someone is to tell them what to do.

clue.text: Decorate after stairs and landing area

indicators.note: after places the word for decorate behind the word for stairs

parts.note: a flight is a set of stairs
to deck is to adorn, as in deck the halls

explanation.surface: Doing up the stairs and the landing at home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'landing' suggests the top of the stairs, but it is where aircraft land on a carrier.
explanation.definitionFit: The deck of an aircraft carrier where planes take off and touch down is a landing area.

clue.text: Tax protester who presented her buff form

definitions.text: Tax protester who presented her buff form

parts.words: Tax protester who presented her buff form
parts.note: the legendary lady who rode naked through Coventry to get her husband to lift a tax

explanation.surface: A protester who handed in a buff-coloured tax form.
explanation.walkthrough: Buff forms suggest official paperwork; 'in the buff' means naked. Legend says Lady Godiva rode naked through Coventry in protest at a tax.
explanation.definitionFit: The legendary Coventry noblewoman rode naked to protest her husband's taxes on the townsfolk.

clue.text: Show great respect to tug having raised Chinese vessel first

indicators.note: first tells us the raised piece comes at the start
raised in a down clue means the word is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: a wok is a Chinese cooking pan
to tow is to tug along

explanation.surface: Showing respect to a tugboat that has hoisted a Chinese ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns WOK into KOW; 'vessel' suggests a ship but is a pan.
explanation.definitionFit: To kowtow is to kneel and bow low before someone, showing deep deference.

clue.text: Placed a number on benefit

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty
aid is help or benefit, as in state aid

explanation.surface: Putting a figure on welfare payments.
explanation.definitionFit: To have laid something down is to have placed it.

clue.text: This plant requires proper drainage

indicators.note: proper suggests setting things right, so the letters of drainage are rearranged

explanation.surface: A gardening tip: this shrub needs good drainage.
explanation.definitionFit: The gardenia is a fragrant flowering shrub, so it is a plant.

clue.text: In hostilities I have a get-out

indicators.note: In places a piece inside another word

parts.note: war is open hostilities
I have shortened is I've

explanation.surface: In wartime someone claims to have an escape route.
explanation.definitionFit: A clause excusing someone from an obligation is a get-out from it.

clue.text: Begrudged having to compete in the final round

indicators.note: in places one word inside another

parts.note: the end is the final part
to vie is to compete

explanation.surface: Resentful at having to play in the last round.
explanation.definitionFit: To have envied someone is to have resented their good fortune.

clue.text: It's associated with head and tails

definitions.text: It's associated with head and tails

parts.words: It's associated with head and tails
parts.note: formal headgear worn on the head with a tailcoat, not the sides of a coin

explanation.surface: Something to do with tossing a coin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head and tails' suggests a coin toss; tails is a tailcoat.
explanation.definitionFit: The tall silk hat goes on the head and is worn with a tailcoat at formal events.
